answer: Cross-Epoch Neighbour Retention Rule. Each epoch, an identity hashes its counterparties into fixed buckets and commits to the bucket set; the next epoch must overlap the prior set above a rising threshold. Buckets form a trellis over time, so a clone farm must sustain the same partner mix across epochs rather than spin up fresh links. A velvet-smooth single-epoch turnout cannot fake retained neighbours. The horizon for overlap grows each cycle, forcing attackers to buy genuine recurring activity that compounds per identity rather than pay once.
